elements.quote: The purpose of this systematic review is to evaluate the efficacy of tracheal tube introducers and stylets for ETI in the prehospital setting.
elements.reason: The abstract explicitly identifies the report as a systematic review.

elements.quote: The purpose of this systematic review is to evaluate the efficacy of tracheal tube introducers and stylets for ETI in the prehospital setting.
elements.reason: The main objective/review question is stated in the Purpose section.
The abstract does not specify the main inclusion and exclusion criteria.

elements.quote: A literature search was conducted on the 2nd of March 2021 across PubMed, Embase (Ovid) and the Cochrane Central Register of Controlled Trials (CENTRAL) to identify relevant studies.
elements.reason: The abstract identifies the information sources (databases) and the search date.
The abstract states a quality assessment was performed, but it does not specify the methods used to assess risk of bias.

elements.quote: Included studies had their data extracted and both a quality assessment and statistical analysis were performed.
elements.reason: The abstract indicates that quality assessment and statistical analysis were performed, but it does not describe the specific methods used to present and synthesize results (e.g., model type, effect measures).
The abstract does not report the total number of included studies and participants, nor does it summarize relevant study characteristics with those totals.

elements.quote: Results The summary estimate of prehospital studies with video technology showed a statistically significant increase in first pass ETI success in favour of bougies (RR 1.15, CI 1.10-1.21, p < 0.0001). The summary estimates of prehospital studies without video technology and simulation studies with and without video technology showed no statistical difference between methods for first pass or overall ETI success.
elements.reason: Main outcomes and effect estimates are reported, but the abstract does not provide the number of included studies and participants for each outcome.

elements.quote: The summary estimate of prehospital studies with video technology showed a statistically significant increase in first pass ETI success in favour of bougies (RR 1.15, CI 1.10-1.21, p < 0.0001).
elements.reason: A meta-analytic summary estimate (RR) with a confidence interval is reported.

elements.quote: The summary estimate of prehospital studies with video technology showed a statistically significant increase in first pass ETI success in favour of bougies (RR 1.15, CI 1.10-1.21, p < 0.0001).
elements.reason: The abstract states direction of effect and which group is favored (bougies).
The abstract does not briefly summarize important limitations of the included evidence.

elements.quote: Conclusion Both tracheal tube introducers and stylets function as efficacious aids to intubation in the prehospital environment. Where video technology is available, bougies could offer a statistically significant advantage in terms of first pass ETI success. Where video technology is unavailable, a combination of clinical scenario, practitioner expertise and personal preference might ultimately guide the choice of device.
elements.reason: The abstract provides a general interpretation of results and implications for practice.
The abstract does not specify the primary source of funding for the review.
The abstract does not provide the register name and registration number.
No explicit description of the current state of knowledge and important uncertainties is provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to systematically review the literature relevant to the use of bougies and stylets for ETI in the prehospital setting. This should inform a conclusion regarding their prehospital efficacy and allow practitioners to decide whether and how best to incorporate these devices into their practice.
elements.reason: The retrieved text explains the need and importance of conducting the review to inform conclusions about prehospital efficacy and guide practitioner decisions.
The retrieved evidence does not describe how existing similar systematic reviews motivate the current review, nor does it identify/cite prior systematic reviews as updates/replications.
No proposed mechanism of action for the interventions (tracheal tube introducers/bougies vs stylets) is described in the retrieved evidence.
No logic model or hypothesised relationships between intervention components and outcomes are provided in the retrieved evidence.

elements.quote: The aim of this study was to systematically review the literature relevant to the use of bougies and stylets for ETI in the prehospital setting.
elements.reason: The objective/aim is explicitly stated, but it is not clearly formulated as a structured question using a relevant question-formulation framework (e.g., population/exposure/intervention/outcome style question).

No planned intervention comparisons (e.g., between specific device types such as bougie vs stylet) are explicitly stated using PICO (or an appropriate variant). The evidence provided describes outcomes and analysis models but does not present planned comparisons in a PICO-like format.

elements.reason: The evidence provides only a partial beginning of the inclusion criteria (type of studies and general exposure/intervention context), but the full list of eligibility characteristics (e.g., all relevant question-framework components and any follow-up requirements) is not shown in the retrieved text.
No retrieved evidence specifies eligibility criteria for report characteristics such as dissemination year, language, or publication/report status.

elements.quote: Five full-text articles were excluded, two reported the use of a bougie/stylet in an exchange manoeuvre, one reported the use of a stylet without laryngoscope and two did not report bougie/stylet efficacy outcomes at all.
elements.reason: The evidence distinguishes an exclusion reason related to outcomes not being reported (“did not report ... efficacy outcomes at all”), but it does not distinguish this from exclusion due to outcomes not being measured.

elements.quote: Two studies [20, 21] were included in our meta-analysis of bougie versus stylet first pass ETI success for prehospital studies without video technology (Fig. 3) ... Two studies [14, 15] were included in our meta-analysis of bougie versus stylet first pass ETI success for prehospital studies with video technology (Fig. 4). ... Two studies [19, 22] were included in our meta-analysis of bougie versus non-bougie method overall ETI success for simulation studies with video technology (Fig. 6). Four studies [23-26] were included in our meta-analysis of a bougie versus non-bougie method overall ETI success for simulation studies without video technology (Fig. 5).
elements.reason: The retrieved evidence specifies groups/comparisons used within each synthesis (e.g., bougie vs stylet vs non-bougie method, and stratification by prehospital vs simulation and with vs without video technology) and links these to the outcomes analyzed.

elements.quote: This review aimed to focus exclusively on the prehospital efficacy of these devices to guide the practice of prehospital personnel in their unique setting, thus inclusion of hospital-based RCTs was deemed inappropriate.
elements.reason: A rationale is explicitly provided for a restriction on study eligibility (excluding hospital-based RCTs) based on the review’s focus on prehospital efficacy.

elements.quote: Dichotomous outcomes were analysed using risk ratios (RR) as summary statistics. A pooled estimate of RRs and weighted mean differences were computed using the DerSimonian and Laird random effects model [13].

The retrieved evidence does not describe methods for re-expressing synthesized results using another effect measure.

elements.quote: The remaining 14 articles had their full-texts assessed for eligibility. The nine remaining studies had their reference lists screened and a further four studies were identified and included. A total of 13 studies were therefore included in our qualitative synthesis [14-26]. Of these studies, 10 were included in our quantitative synthesis [14, 15, 19-26].
elements.reason: The manuscript describes how studies were assessed for eligibility (title/abstract screening, full-text eligibility assessment, reasons for exclusions, and reference list screening) and reports which eligible studies were included in the qualitative versus quantitative syntheses.

elements.quote: We extracted the following data: (1) characteristics of included studies; (2) first pass ETI success and overall ETI success of included studies.
elements.reason: The review reports what data were extracted for synthesis, but it does not describe methods used to prepare data for presentation/synthesis beyond extraction (e.g., how missing summary statistics were handled or whether any data conversions were performed).

elements.quote: Table 4 summarises the primary outcomes of first pass ETI success and overall ETI success for studies with a simulation design without video technology [17, 18, 23-26].
